value.body: A shipping operations executive works in a shore office, making sure ships move, load and unload as planned. Shipping lines, ship-management firms, port agencies and chartering companies hire them. The day involves coordinating with ships, ports, agents and customers, and keeping voyage documents and costs in order.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Sea experience as an officer, or a degree with a shipping/logistics course

items.label: Common documents
items.value: Bills of lading, port clearance papers, voyage instructions

items.label: Cargo at major ports
items.source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (as reported)

items.label: Non-major ports' share of cargo
items.note: Major and non-major ports together handled ~778 MT in these six months
items.source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Update on Indian Port Sector

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Seafarers often move ashore into operations after some years at sea, where their ship experience is valued. Graduates without sea time usually join as trainees at a port agency or shipping line and learn on the job.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Communication with ports, agents and crews

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: operations manager, chartering, marine superintendent (with sea experience).
Ships run round the clock, so after-hours calls are common.
Shore roles offer a settled life compared with sea contracts.
